correctness.rationale: The Fourier transform follows by subtracting the two odd Cauchy-kernel terms. The Fourier coefficients of the continuous, 1-periodic function e^{-2πitξ}Z(t,ξ) are then exactly the transform at k+ξ; summing its exponential tails gives the stated rational formula. The defining Zak series is C¹, including across the ξ=0 seam, since the ξ-derivative is bounded termwise locally by a summable order-|m|^{-2} bound. All four rational denominators stay nonzero on the unit circle. A separate symbolic calculation from the four cleared terms reproduced the exact reciprocal resultant and both edge and midpoint factorizations, without executing CHECK.py. Real coefficients ensure any unit-circle root is common with the reciprocal. For 0<ξ<1, B is strictly negative. For A, factoring the exponential terms reduces its sign to the difference of the increasing sinh ratios at ξ and 1-ξ. For C, the derivative in the pole parameter reduces to monotonicity of y tanh y, again excluding vanishing except at ξ=1/2. At the midpoint the residual quadratic divided by z has a strictly positive lower bound (1+w²)(1+s²) on the circle; at the edge only z=±1 can vanish. At those real points S_z is positive: it is a difference of increasing functions 2q/(1∓q)² evaluated at q and r on the edge, or of the increasing function √q(1+q)/(1-q)² at the midpoint. S_ξ has signs +,+,- by the stated hyperbolic derivative tests. Thus ∂_t S=2πizS_z yields the three nonzero real Jacobians with signs -,+,+ in the stated orientation. The packaged checker was inspected, not run; finite comparisons of Zak sums are only corroboration. No conclusion outside distinct positive a,b or at other Gabor densities is required.

evidence: Belov–Kulikov–Lyubarskii use rational fractions and a Zak representation for one-sided pole classes. Their near-critical frame criterion assumes a positive real part on the entire circle, not a classification of forced zeros, and their critical-density completeness assertion uses almost-everywhere nonvanishing.
Ghosh fixes x/((x²+1)(x²+4)); the inspected cubic and reflection formulas apply to that window in a rational-density frame problem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: One-sided pole conditions exclude the mixed upper/lower pairs, and almost-everywhere nonvanishing says nothing about the number or multiplicity of isolated zeros. The fixed-ratio formula is an antecedent, not a theorem for arbitrary pole ratios.

originality.rationale: The distinct contribution is the complete simple signed zero set uniformly for two independently placed positive pole pairs. Oddness forces the three candidate points, the rational Zak representation has close precedents, and the same three coordinates in a different window class are not new. Available prior results do not settle exclusion of other zeros or the Jacobian signs over this two-parameter family.
residual_risks: A more general mixed-pole classification outside the inspected statements could subsume the rational result; the literature comparison is not a historical-priority certificate.
The independent symbolic check establishes identities, not sign uniformity or completeness by itself; those depend on the analytic inequalities and unit-circle argument.
